review_notes: The file has one theorem. I read it, the sibling file MovingAmplitudeHarmonicDiagonal.lean, and the definition of movingAmplitudeDiagonal in MovingAmplitudeTerms.lean. I grepped the Arithmetic directory for the distinctive `let : ∀ a : A, Fact (a.1 : ℕ).Prime` line. It appears in six files: this one, HarmonicDiagonal, SupportedHarmonic, SupportedSymmetrization, LiveHarmonic and LiveSymmetrization. Each of the six has the same skeleton, line for line. I did not read the template-level lemmas (movingTemplate_*_diagonal_*) and did not compile anything. The proposed lemma and the definition refactor are untested. In particular, whether the closing `simpa` still unifies after the fibre term is extracted into a definition is unverified. I also did not check whether other files use `unfold movingAmplitudeDiagonal`. The residual `simpa` block differs per variant: Symmetrized variants add `movingSymmetrizedTemplateCoefficient`. I therefore propose factoring only the common outer skeleton and leaving the `simpa` conversion in each theorem.

findings.problem: The proof opens with the same skeleton as five sibling theorems: `unfold movingAmplitudeDiagonal; dsimp only; apply Finset.sum_le_sum; intro u _; apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left _ (mul_nonneg …); apply Finset.sum_le_sum; intro p _; apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left _ (hφ0 _)`. It then states the same two `Fact … Prime` instances and ends with a `simpa only [movingTemplateTransferWeight, movingAmplitudePrior, movingOneGiant_transform_tagged, ρ, ν, α, θ, Nat.cast_prod, Function.comp_def] using hd`. The mathematical content of the skeleton is a termwise comparison. It reduces the diagonal to a bound on each (u,p) fibre term, using nonnegativity of ∏ μ, of the cast ℕ-product, and of φ. The same reduction is copied in HarmonicDiagonal, SupportedHarmonic, SupportedSymmetrization, LiveHarmonic and LiveSymmetrization. Only the template lemma name, the `hν` argument and one extra simp lemma (`movingSymmetrizedTemplateCoefficient`) differ between them. A change to the definition of `movingAmplitudeDiagonal` would force six parallel edits.
findings.proposed_change:
1. In MovingAmplitudeTerms.lean, split the fibre term out of `movingAmplitudeDiagonal` into a def, e.g. `movingAmplitudeFibreDiagonal … u p : ℝ := (pivotDiagonal (fun a => X a * ∏ i, value (y a i)) v (fun a => W u p a * movingTaggedTransform …)).re`, with the `let`s inlined. Then set `movingAmplitudeDiagonal … = ∑ u, (∏ i, μ n (u i)) * (∏ i, value (u i) : ℕ) * ∑ p ∈ I, φ (Real.log p - G (n+1)) * movingAmplitudeFibreDiagonal … u p`.
2. Prove once: `theorem movingAmplitudeDiagonal_le_of_fibre {σ} [Fintype σ] … (hμ : ∀ j a, 0 ≤ μ j a) (hφ0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ φ x) (B : (TreeLeafIndex n × Fin 4 → σ) → ℕ → ℝ) (hB : ∀ u p, movingAmplitudeFibreDiagonal … u p ≤ B u p) : movingAmplitudeDiagonal … ≤ ∑ u, (∏ i, μ n (u i)) * (∏ i, value (u i) : ℕ) * ∑ p ∈ I, φ (Real.log p - G (n+1)) * B u p`. The proof is the current skeleton: `unfold movingAmplitudeDiagonal; refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun u _ => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (Finset.sum_le_sum fun p _ => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hB u p) (hφ0 _)) (mul_nonneg (Finset.prod_nonneg fun i _ => hμ n (u i)) (Nat.cast_nonneg _))`.
3. Rewrite each of the six theorems as `refine movingAmplitudeDiagonal_le_of_fibre … (fun u p => ?_)`, followed by only the variant-specific part: `have hd := movingTemplate_symmetrized_harmonic_diagonal_le … hν u p …`, the two Fact lets, and the `simpa … using hd`. The skeleton lines 41–50 then disappear from all six files.
 If the definition refactor is unwanted, the lemma can instead state `hB` directly on the unfolded `(pivotDiagonal …).re` expression, at the cost of a longer statement.
findings.benefit: The termwise-comparison argument sits in one lemma, so a future change to `movingAmplitudeDiagonal` or to its nonnegativity hypotheses is made once, not in six files. Each wrapper theorem is shortened to its real content. That content is which template bound is applied and how its coefficient is unfolded. A reader can then see how the Harmonic, Supported, Live and Symmetrized variants differ without diffing near-identical scripts.
